draft.title: Lines of good fit
card: A line of good fit is a straight line drawn by eye through a scatterplot that shows a linear trend. It follows the general direction of the points.
Draw it so that about half the points lie above the line and half below. The points should be spread fairly evenly along it. The line does not need to touch any point.
To predict, pick a value on the horizontal axis. Go up to the line, then across to the vertical axis and read off the value.
Example: a line passes through (2, 10) and (6, 30). At x = 4, the line is at y = 20, the midway value. So the prediction is 20.
draft.remember: Draw the line by eye through the middle of the points, then read predictions off it.

a.q: Which describes a well-drawn line of good fit?
opts: It follows the trend, with points spread on both sides
It joins the first point to the last point
It passes through as many points as possible
It lies below all of the points
a.why: A good line follows the trend and has about half the points on each side. Joining the first and last points is tempting, but this can leave most points on one side. Touching many points is not required.
a.clue: Think about how the points should sit around the line.

b.q: Kai draws a line of good fit that passes through (10, 50) and (30, 90). What does the line predict when x = 20?
b.why: At x = 20, the line is midway between x = 10 and x = 30. The midway value of y is (50 + 90) ÷ 2 = 70. The value 60 comes from adding only 10 to 50, which does not match the line's steepness.
b.clue: x = 20 is exactly halfway between 10 and 30.

a.best: It follows the trend, with points spread on both sides
